story_clusters.headline: Angus Taylor unveils Liberal shadow cabinet after leadership victory
story_clusters.summary: New Liberal leader Angus Taylor announced his shadow ministry, appointing Tim Wilson as shadow treasurer and promoting conservative allies while demoting supporters of former leader Sussan Ley. The reshuffle aims to rebuild the Coalition's economic credentials and pursue a more rightwing agenda focused on immigration and traditional values.

story_clusters.headline: Albanese government refuses to help ISIS families return to Australia from Syria
story_clusters.summary: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese declared the government would not assist 34 women and children with ISIS links trying to return from Syrian camps, despite legal obligations to allow citizens back. The stance sparked political debate with opposition calling for stronger passport restrictions and accusations of inconsistency from Liberal senators.

story_clusters.headline: RBA under pressure as strong labour data fuels expectations of further rate hikes
story_clusters.summary: The Reserve Bank of Australia faces mounting pressure to raise interest rates again after January unemployment remained at 4.1% and wages growth stayed elevated. RBA minutes revealed the board saw a 'material shift' in the economic outlook, with economists split on whether another hike will come in March or May.

story_clusters.headline: Australia commits $3.9 billion for AUKUS submarine facility in Adelaide
story_clusters.summary: Prime Minister Albanese announced a $3.9 billion 'down payment' for the Osborne submarine construction facility in South Australia, part of a total $30 billion project to eventually build nuclear-powered submarines under the AUKUS partnership with the US and UK. The announcement came as HMS Anson made a historic visit to Perth.

story_clusters.headline: Anthony Albanese comments on Prince Andrew arrest as 'extraordinary fall from grace'
story_clusters.summary: Prime Minister Albanese described the arrest of Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor (formerly Prince Andrew) on his 66th birthday as an 'extraordinary fall from grace' but declined to suggest Australia should reassess its ties with the British monarchy. The comments came during political interviews where he also addressed other domestic issues.
